clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: An adult with sepsis initially receives broad empiric antimicrobial therapy. Culture and susceptibility results later identify one susceptible bacterial pathogen. Which change best reflects current de-escalation guidance?

options.A: Stop unnecessary agents or narrow therapy to target the identified susceptible pathogen.
options.B: Continue every empiric antimicrobial for the full course despite results showing several are unnecessary.
options.C: Broaden antimicrobial coverage after susceptibility testing identifies a narrower effective option.
options.D: Ignore susceptibility results because de-escalation is reserved for cases with negative cultures.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign recommends antimicrobial de-escalation when a confirmed microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available. The guideline defines de-escalation as discontinuing unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or narrowing the antimicrobial spectrum when appropriate. Therefore, once culture and susceptibility results identify a susceptible pathogen, unnecessary empiric agents should be stopped or the regimen narrowed rather than maintaining or broadening avoidable coverage.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: When microbiology identifies a susceptible pathogen in sepsis, support antimicrobial de-escalation by stopping unnecessary agents or narrowing therapy appropriately.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, kept all choices as parallel antimicrobial-management actions, and anchored the correct answer to the 2026 SSC definition of de-escalation.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Antimicrobial Therapy — de-escalation recommendation and remarks
audit_findings_append.finding: The original construct was clinically correct but one distractor used absolute wording. The revised item directly tests de-escalation after susceptibility results with concise parallel options.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the guideline definition of de-escalation after microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility data.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Continuing unnecessary agents contradicts de-escalation and prolongs avoidable exposure.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Broadening therapy despite a narrower susceptible option is the opposite of de-escalation.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. The strongest recommendation specifically applies when a microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone applies the guideline-defined de-escalation action to the culture and susceptibility results in the stem.
cueing_check: All four choices are antimicrobial-regimen changes of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
